title: Your number map, explained without the fog
intro: Two key numbers from your birth date, a lasting profile, and a fresh focus every week. Everything is calculated on your device.
freeTitle: Readings like this are often sold as a separate consultation
freeText: Here the core map, explanations, and weekly reading are free. Your result opens immediately—no account, phone number, or payment screen at the end.
name: What should we call you?
nameHint: Use any alphabet. Your name is only used in the greeting and never changes the calculation.
birthHint: The day gives the consciousness number; the full date gives the mission number.
birthTimeHint: If you know it, we add a separate daily-rhythm note. Your core Syutsai numbers stay the same.
privacy: Your name, date, time, and test results stay on this device.
coreRule: The Syutsai core comes from the birth date. We do not turn your name into a number or mix birth time into the core values. Extra layers are always labeled.
horoscopeText: We show your Sun sign for reference. A full natal chart also needs exact time and birthplace, so it belongs in a separate section.
sharedResult: Someone shared this result with you
newWeek: Your new weekly reading is ready
core: This is your general profile, not a forecast: consciousness number {consciousness} describes your usual way of seeing and choosing; mission number {mission} points to a longer direction for your potential.
shadow: When a strength goes too far
matrixStrongHint: A repeat highlights a theme in your date. It does not mean better or worse.
matrixMissingHint: Missing digits are not flaws. They point to qualities that may grow through experience rather than switch on automatically.
matrixBalanced: No digit repeats more than once
fromTests: BASED ON ACTIONS, NOT THE DATE
behaviorText: Your other test answers put {top} first, with {second} as the second anchor. This layer makes the advice more specific without pretending to be Syutsai.
behaviorEmpty: For now we only see your number map. Take two or three tests and this section will add a second layer based on your real answers, not only your date.
rhythmNote: This practical rhythm does not change either core number and is not presented as a canonical Syutsai formula.
rhythmEmpty: Know your exact birth time? Add it for a separate note about a comfortable daily rhythm.
zodiacNote: Shown for reference and not used in the Syutsai calculation.
weeklyLayerHint: The plain-language summary comes first. Your lasting map and the formulas are below.
how: How this works and where the limits are
howText: The consciousness number is the digital root of the birth day. The mission number is the digital root of all birth-date digits. Year, month, and week are an open adapted layer that compares the current cycle with your lasting map and, when available, answers from other tests.
nameTimeRule: The name is only used in the greeting. Birth time adds a separate rhythm note but does not change the core numbers. The zodiac sign is shown as a separate reference.
disclaimer: Syutsai, number cycles, and horoscopes are esoteric interpretations for entertainment and reflection. They are not scientific psychological assessment, medical advice, or a guarantee of events.
weekFormulaNote: The five numbers are separated: two are lasting and three are temporary. Your overall profile does not change when a new week begins.

relationLabels.conflict: the week challenges your usual pace

profileTexts.decision: A “{mind}” mind first looks for an answer that feels clear inside. A “{mission}” mission adds a second check: does this choice move you in the right direction, or only remove today's discomfort?
profileTexts.work: At work, combine your natural “{mind}” style with the longer “{mission}” direction. One role that needs both qualities is healthier than constantly trying to copy someone else's pace.
profileTexts.communication: In conversation you naturally lead with “{mind}” and gradually learn to add “{mission}”. People understand you better when expectations are spoken rather than left as a test they do not know they are taking.
profileTexts.money: Money choices feel steadier when “{mind}” checks the present and “{mission}” checks the longer purpose. A quick desire and long-term value are not the same thing.

1.title: The Starter
1.core: You spot a starting point quickly and would rather shape events than wait for permission.
1.shadow: Under stress, independence can turn into bluntness and resistance to feedback.
1.resource: A clear personal goal and one small first step restore momentum.
1.simple: Someone who finds it easier to start, take ownership, and set direction.

2.title: The Diplomat
2.core: You read the room, notice relationship details, and connect people without making a show of it.
2.shadow: You may adapt for too long, store resentment, and hope others will guess what you need.
2.resource: A calm conversation, a trusted partner, and permission not to answer instantly help.
2.simple: Someone who reads people well and can reach agreement without pressure.

3.title: The Guide
3.core: Meaning, learning, and making complex ideas understandable are natural sources of strength.
3.shadow: Theory can become lecturing, perfectionism, or promises too large for the day.
3.resource: Learning, a clear plan, and passing useful knowledge forward restore you.
3.simple: Someone who enjoys learning, explaining, and helping others see a clear path.

4.title: The Builder
4.core: You see how systems work, notice weak points, and can turn chaos into a reliable process.
4.shadow: Order can become control, suspicion, or endless correction of small details.
4.resource: Clear boundaries, a definition of done, and visible order around you help.
4.simple: Someone who likes creating order and understanding how everything connects.

5.title: The Connector
5.core: You adapt fast, link people and ideas, and explain things in a lively, accessible way.
5.shadow: Novelty can scatter attention or sell the idea before the foundation is tested.
5.resource: Movement, a fresh conversation, and a short experiment with a deadline restore energy.
5.simple: Someone who starts conversations, connects people, and explains things plainly.

6.title: The Harmonizer
6.core: You value quality of life, beauty, closeness, and spaces where people feel cared for.
6.shadow: Care can slide into control, approval-seeking, or spending to create an impression.
6.resource: Unshowy beauty, physical comfort, and relationships with mutual care help.
6.simple: Someone who wants the space around them to feel beautiful, calm, and kind.

7.title: The Researcher
7.core: You need to reach the root, test the logic, and have quiet before naming your conclusion.
7.shadow: Depth can become withdrawal, overthinking, or treating distance as safety.
7.resource: Solo focus, a deep problem, and time without information noise restore you.
7.simple: Someone who dislikes shallow answers and wants to reach the root independently.

8.title: The Strategist
8.core: You see scale, the real price of choices, and how to gather resources around an ambitious goal.
8.shadow: Results can become the only measure of worth, with pressure or status-driven risk.
8.resource: Clear numbers, ownership of your choice, and a goal useful beyond yourself help.
8.simple: Someone who looks several steps ahead and can count resources and consequences.

9.title: The Completer
9.core: You see the larger picture, the human meaning, and how to close a cycle so the next can begin.
9.shadow: You may rescue everyone, dramatize endings, or hold the past out of duty.
9.resource: A promise completed, a useful action, and permission to release finished work restore you.
9.simple: Someone who sees the whole picture, draws a conclusion, and makes room for what comes next.

night.title: Quiet start.
night.text: Important work may feel easier after private preparation; schedule people after you have found your own focus.

morning.title: Early momentum.
morning.text: Put demanding thinking in the first half of the day before other people's tasks divide your attention.

day.title: Daytime pace.
day.text: Movement, contact, and visible progress help; split long solo tasks into shorter stages.

evening.title: Late synthesis.
evening.text: Ideas may connect more easily later in the day, but important promises still deserve a night's sleep.

texts.theme: The main focus is {theme}. Your lasting “{mind}” style is still there; this week simply asks you to add another tool and choose one visible or measurable action.
texts.boost: This week's theme naturally supports your usual way of working. Spend that advantage on one meaningful start rather than ten small tasks.
texts.compensation: The week asks for a pace that may not switch on automatically. Give it one short, controlled block and decide in advance what counts as enough.
texts.neutral: There is no strong tension between your map and the week. A clear priority and boundaries matter more than a good mood or a random sign.
texts.conflict: Your usual style and the week's pace pull in different directions. Take one reversible test step before deciding whether to speed up.
texts.work: Fit {score}/10. Work asks for “{theme}”, while your natural approach is “{mind}”. Name one result you can show by week's end and time-box preparation.
texts.money: Fit {score}/10, but this is not an income prediction. Check the price, the effect one month from now, and whether the choice can be reversed; take numbers into important talks.
texts.relationships: Fit {score}/10. In a “{theme}” week, one direct conversation helps: say what you want, ask how the other person sees it, and do not invent their answer.
texts.decisions: Fit {score}/10. Turn reversible choices into small experiments; check expensive, public, and long-term choices against facts and give them one pressure-free night.
texts.energy: Energy fit {score}/10. Work in waves: an important block, a short break, then simple tasks. Fatigue is a signal to lower load, not proof that you chose the wrong path.
texts.risk: The strength of “{mind}” can become too much: overpreparing, controlling every detail, or carrying the whole task alone. Ask: “What is already good enough?”
texts.window: Look for a task where “{mind}” meets “{theme}”. Give it a day, a person, or a measurable result, or the opportunity will remain a nice thought.
texts.avoid: Do not start five things from anxiety, promise under pressure, or treat someone else's urgency as your priority. Pause before an irreversible choice.
texts.mode: One main result, one honest conversation, and one obligation-free evening. That is not too little; it is how a week avoids disappearing into preparation.
texts.joke: Weekly kryptonite: “one more tab, one more reading, and then I will start.” Spoiler: the tab has already multiplied.
texts.why4: Leading trait from your test answers: {top} — {value}%

digestText: This week gives the strongest support to {first} and {second}. The main theme is {theme}.
powerMoment: A GOOD MOMENT FOR WHAT MATTERS
powerMomentHint: Place one important conversation or first step here. It is a planning cue, not a promise of luck.
scoreGuideTitle: The score shows fit with your usual style—it is not a grade for you
scoreGuideText: A higher number means the weekly theme is easier to use in this area. A lower number does not mean failure; slow down and check your choices.
permanentBelowHint: It explains your general style and does not change every week.

work.opportunity: Finish or show one visible result—it matters more now than a long preparation phase.
work.caution: Do not adopt someone else’s urgency or promise more than one week can hold.

money.opportunity: A useful time to recalculate terms, discuss price, or remove an unnecessary expense.
money.caution: Do not buy or agree only for quick relief or to create an impression.

relationships.opportunity: One honest conversation can clear more tension than several days of guessing.
relationships.caution: Do not answer for the other person or treat silence as a finished answer.

decisions.opportunity: Take one small reversible step—it will create more clarity than another round of thinking.
decisions.caution: Check expensive and long-term choices against facts and give them one night.

energy.opportunity: Use your best charge for one important task and leave simple work for a quieter period.
energy.caution: Do not confuse fatigue with inability or play hero on an empty battery.

termHints.consciousness: The number of your birth day. In plain language: how you usually read a situation and what you want first.
termHints.mission: The sum of the full birth date. In this system, a direction that unfolds gradually through experience.
termHints.matrixStrong: Digits that appear more than once in the date. They mark a theme that repeats often.
termHints.matrixMissing: Digits absent from the date. They are not flaws, but qualities that may grow through experience.
termHints.behavior: A conclusion based on your real answers in the app’s other tests.

traitHints.analytical: You like to understand first, compare facts, and find the cause.
traitHints.technical: You work comfortably with devices, mechanisms, exact rules, and clear systems.
traitHints.creative: You notice unusual options and enjoy making something new.
traitHints.social: You read people well and gain energy from useful connection.
traitHints.enterprising: You spot an opening quickly and are ready to take the first step.
traitHints.organizing: You like order, clear roles, and a practical plan.
traitHints.practical: You prefer a concrete result that can be seen or checked.
traitHints.balance: You consider different sides and avoid rushing into extremes.
traitHints.flexibility: You change your approach easily when the situation changes.
